values: Material 1｜Eight fictional paper samples, work orders and blank forms

Paper version P1. Prepare paper, pencil and a millimetre ruler; each sample consists of two rectangles, paper A and paper B, of 60×40mm, with the origin at the lower-left corner, x to the right and y upward. Draw the rectangles and cross marks with the ruler, stack the same-numbered sheets edge-aligned and check the marks; it can be completed without glue. All A marks are at coordinates (30,20)mm; the B marks are: sample 1 (30,20), sample 2 (31,20), sample 3 (28,20), sample 4 (30.5,20), sample 5 (31,20), sample 6 (28.5,20), sample 7 (33,20), sample 8 (32,20), all in mm. Here the “centre mark” is an alignment mark, and the B mark may deviate from the geometric centre; the horizontal deviation is |B's x − 30|, and all y values are the same. It can be computed from the given coordinates or observed by hand drawing with a ruler; screen/print scaling is not a 1:1 gauge, and a screenshot must not be measured directly as the given value. If the hand drawing deviates from the target, record the actual observation and the difference separately, and do not quietly alter the original input.

Labels: samples 1–8 all carry material paper A/paper B, batch P1 and the corresponding number. The fictional work orders F01/F02/F03/F04/F06/F07/F08 correspond to samples 1/2/3/4/6/7/8 respectively, and each order states material paper A/paper B, batch P1, quantity 1 pairs, 60×40mm, A mark (30,20)mm and horizontal deviation ≤2mm; these fields are complete on seven orders. Sample 5 has only a label and coordinates, with no F05 work order, and must not be fabricated from the general rule. The blank inspection sheet copies the eight rows, numbered 1–8; each row records: label material/batch｜work order number or missing｜given B coordinates｜computed deviation mm｜actual hand-drawn observation (optional)｜whether the work order is complete｜paper-only classification｜next step｜record time｜handoff recipient. The handoff recipient is fixed in the exercise as “simulated reviewer”, and the time is the actual exercise time. This page provides only fictional paper-sample rules and no real adhesive, equipment parameters, SDS or industrial quality standards.
Material 2｜Item-by-item inspection and anomaly handoff

Within 45 minutes, first fill in the eight-row blank sheet of material 1 independently. Verify the label against the corresponding work order first, then compute the horizontal deviation item by item from the given coordinates; a deviation ≤2mm with a complete corresponding work order is recorded as “meets the paper condition”, a missing work order as “pending confirmation”, and a deviation >2mm as “paper rule not met”. The latter two categories are marked as segregated on paper and handed to the simulated reviewer; no order may be added and no real product release may be written. Optional hand drawing serves only as a separate observation exercise and does not override the given-coordinate record.

Output a handoff summary: prompt version P1, the sample numbers and work orders, the observation/computation basis, the missing or over-limit data, the paper classification and the items requiring confirmation by the simulated reviewer; if there is no real root-cause evidence, retain it as unknown. After completing the independent record, read material 3 and note item by item the original conclusion, the reference basis and whether a change is needed.
Material 3｜Reference results and item-by-item review

Given-coordinate deviations: sample 1 0mm, sample 2 1mm, sample 3 2mm, sample 4 0.5mm, sample 5 1mm, sample 6 1.5mm, sample 7 3mm, sample 8 2mm. Check item by item: 1/F01, 2/F02, 3/F03, 4/F04, 6/F06, 8/F08 have complete material, batch, quantity and mark fields and are ≤2mm, so they are recorded as meeting the paper condition only; sample 3 and sample 8 equal the limit and also meet it. Sample 5, even with a deviation of 1mm, remains pending confirmation because it has no work order and must not be guessed or filled in; 7/F07 has a complete work order but 3mm > 2mm, so the paper rule is not met. Samples 5 and 7 are segregated on paper and handed to the simulated reviewer; the six conforming samples do not extrapolate to industrial conformity, real equipment capability or release.

Review each row against the original work order and coordinates, the absolute-value calculation, the equality signs, the classification, the time and the handoff recipient. If the hand-drawn observation differs from the given value, record the drawing error separately and do not use it to change the prompt answer. The unknowns include the real material performance, equipment parameters, cause, SDS and actual product standard; repair, parameter-change or energy-control steps must not be invented.

All work orders, batches and coordinates are editorial fictional inputs, neither industrial specifications nor safety training, real production or quality approval.
